question: Should governments add a per-item levy to ultra-cheap fast fashion?
answer: Clothes this cheap push their costs onto others: landfill, burned stock, polluted rivers and bales of waste exported to poorer countries. A levy on each item folds some of that cost into the price, slows the flood of throwaway pieces and funds collection. French lawmakers have already voted for a penalty of this kind.
move: Whichever side you took, the hinge is whether price or use drives the waste.
ask: Am I judging what I buy by price or by how much I will actually use it?
counterpoint: A flat charge per item falls hardest on the poorest buyers, for whom cheap clothes are the budget, not a luxury. It targets price rather than harm: an expensive garment can be worn as rarely as a cheap one. Online orders cross borders easily, so durability rules, takeback duties and honest labels would reach the waste more directly.
reference: Assemblée nationale, proposition de loi visant à réduire l'impact environnemental de l'industrie textile, adopted at first reading, March 2024
